extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: A benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation, comprising 1,825 diverse tasks across nine domains to evaluate LLMs on interactive visual artifacts.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.citeAs: Tencent Hunyuan Team. ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation. 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Tasks were curated via a multi-stage pipeline combining expert sourcing with LLM generation and refinement. Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots. Automated filters were applied to drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. De-duplication was performed using MinHash, semantic similarity, and screenshot perceptual hashing. Prompts were rewritten by experts and LLMs, with human verification. Checklists were LLM-drafted and human-refined. Solvability was validated by collecting candidate solutions and pruning underspecified items.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two-stage filtering for de-duplication and contamination control using MinHash, semantic similarity, and screenshot perceptual hashing. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Prompts were rewritten for clarity/completeness/executability. Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models. Checklists were generated and calibrated.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. De-duplication was performed using MinHash, semantic similarity over prompts/checklists/normalized DOM/CSS/JS, and screenshot perceptual hashing. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed. Execution was standardized using headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1024x768 resolution with deterministic seeds.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were LLM-drafted and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and achieved Cohen’s κ≥0.8 among annotators. The checklist items are grouped into five vision-oriented and five code-oriented dimensions. Scoring is performed by a Multimodal LLM (MLLM)-as-Judge (dual-referee: Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B) guided by the checklist.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A 10% manually curated seed was used for calibration, achieving Cohen’s κ≥0.8 among annotators. The seed is reused as few-shot references to keep difficulty high and rubrics consistent. Human validation was conducted on 280 instances with pairwise agreement up to 90.95%.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to provide a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models. It addresses the bottleneck in evaluating visual fidelity and interactive integrity, which are central to user experience in modern applications.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior by capturing and analyzing a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions. The benchmark focuses on evaluating the quality of the final artifact generated in a single turn and does not assess agentic capabilities like iterative refinement or self-debugging.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Usage Guidelines: The benchmark is designed for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifacts, assessing visual fidelity, interactive correctness, and code quality. It supports fine-grained capability analysis across difficulty tiers (Easy/Medium/Hard) and task categories.
